heard: A 50-foot steel tank in Boston was leaking 2,300,000 gallons. In 1919, the owners ignored obvious structural cracks to save money. On a warm winter day, the structure ruptured in the north end. A 35-mile-per-hour wave killed at least 21 people. To hide the leaks, the company had simply painted it brown. No one was ever charged for the 50-foot steel tank leaking.
